cases.root_cause: A short IBKR market-data/connectivity blip at the 09:10 slot: the data farm dropped (`2103`), so the run could not get SPX's spot price at 09:14:48, and the slot that opened at 09:20:05–09:20:17 hit a socket disconnect and connect timeouts. It recovered by itself within one slot — 78/78 option slots (100% coverage) succeeded in the session — so no action is needed.

Alpaca answered every 2026-10-15 equity_bars run successfully, but 700 of the expected 3,900 5-min bars for the session were never delivered by the vendor (no errors, no quarantine, ~2 missing bars per symbol across 350 symbols): a vendor data gap, not a collector failure. The gap is not recovered: the 17:30 eod refetch of the session still returned rows=3200 / missing_bars=700 while the nine other refetched sessions returned rows=3900 / missing_bars=0, so those bars are absent from staged/ and the SLI-3 figure of 100% is a measurement artifact, not proof of complete data.

The data does not support a specific cause. On 2026-10-16 both the option_snapshots and index_snapshots runs that started at 09:10:02 ET failed together after 4 s with a bare TimeoutError(), then the 09:15 and every later slot ran normally; the 09:10 slot's data was lost. A single 4-second timeout affecting both datasets at the same opening slot, with no IBKR error codes recorded, no secdef stall, no 1100/2103 farm-disconnect codes and no Gateway restart, is most consistent with a one-off connectivity/request timeout at the Gateway at the open (a transient blip), but the run records do not show the IBKR codes or Gateway state that would pin it down; subsequent runs recovered on their own, so no reconnect is warranted.

Both IBKR snapshot collectors failed at 09:10:02 ET with TimeoutError() after only ~4s (option_snapshots and index_snapshots), i.e. requests hanging with no data returned rather than a clean refusal. No snapshot runs succeeded between ~09:50 and 10:41, and scheduled slots ahead of that ran late (the option book's gap_s at the failed slot is ~62,101 s, i.e. ~17.3 h, showing the scheduled__2026-10-16T13:10:00 slot effectively sat unserved and downstream slots queued behind it). This pattern — hanging requests, queued slots, no new data — matches the IBKR contract-definition (secdef) / request-hang failure mode documented in runbooks/gateway section A/B and in incidents/2026-10-23, not a gateway restart and not a data-farm disconnect (no 1100/2103/2105/2157 codes appear on any run). The 10:09:43 equity_bars failure (RemoteProtocolError, Alpaca) is a separate vendor-side blip, not the cause of the snapshot gap.

The 10:09:43 equity_bars run died with RemoteProtocolError('Server disconnected without sending a response.') after 18 s — a transient Alpaca vendor disconnect. It cost no data: SLI 3 for 2026-10-16 is 100% (3900/3900 bars) and the 17:30 ET eod refetch recovered every session. The same day's real incident was an IBKR 1100 connectivity loss around 10:10 ET that hung a request and made option/index slots late (SLI 2 60.26% vs 95%), though SLI 1 coverage stayed 100%.

The 09:20:01 option snapshot run was killed at 480 s with no error message: it hit the run's execution timeout/6-min run budget (the run-budget ceiling) rather than a Gateway fault, and the slot was then retried; the session still met coverage (SLI 1 100%).

Codes 10090 and 10167 (with 354) are market-data-permission codes on the collector username, not a Gateway or farm fault: 354/10090 mean "not subscribed for this instrument" and 10167 means IBKR is serving delayed rather than live data. Runs on 2026-10-19 did not fail on them — they logged the codes but returned rows; the only failure that day was a separate 09:20:01 option_snapshots run. This is a subscription/entitlement problem, which self-healing and RECONNECTDATA cannot fix.

Monitoring artifact, not a data loss: runs for 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 are not recorded in this host's pipeline_runs (collection ran on the Mac host before the ~2026-10-27 move to the Windows host), so ops/slo.md's rule that a session with no runs counts as uncovered makes slo_status report 0% option coverage for those sessions. The data exists: 10-23 is documented at 100% SLI 1 (secdef stall 10:35-11:00 delayed 4 slots, no option slot lost), and equity bars read 3900/3900 for both days.

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) server stopped answering for about 5 minutes at 10:35 ET. Every run then asked it for the underlying contract and listed expirations (qualifyContracts / reqSecDefOptParams) before any quote request, so the index run was killed by its 2-min execution timeout and lost both attempts, while the option run's hung first request (RequestTimeout = 300 s) ate its 6-min budget and failed the slot, whose retry succeeded 7 min late and pushed the next four slots back. The Gateway itself was healthy: no data-farm errors, quotes kept flowing. Fixed by the 08:15 contract_cache refresh (c2dd697) and dropping snapshot retries (d0f3b5d).

The IB Gateway froze for the whole 2026-10-26 session: the 08:15 ET contract_cache refresh re-listed every cached expiry (~23.7 MB / 23,376 messages), which overloaded IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service, broke the hfarm data farm and then wedged the Gateway until 09:16, after which its API port accepted no connections at all. The collectors therefore failed every option slot; the only heal attempt (09:02 gateway check) never ran because its hung request raised past check_gateway's healing path, IBC's RESTART could not restart a wedged Gateway, and the container restart plus 2FA login only happened at 19:39-19:40 ET, after the close. Option snapshots cannot be backfilled, so the session is permanently lost.

The 09:10 option and index runs on both days died on a ~4 s connect TimeoutError that recovered on the next slot, but the identical symptom does not establish a common cause and the two days fall on opposite sides of the ef762db contract_cache fix. 2026-10-27 sits inside the documented 10-28→11-02 morning secdef/Gateway stall window (runbooks/gateway; incidents/2026-10-26), so its 09:10 connect timeout is plausibly that known pattern. 2026-10-30 is after the fix for that root cause, so the same symptom there is not supported as the same mechanism. Neither day has farm codes, gateway-check results or the 09:00-09:20 logs in the tool data, so the shared trigger is undetermined.

On 2026-11-05 the option run's 1100 (connectivity lost) was followed by 1102 (restored) and the 2103 farm break by a 2110 (farm restored, data maintained) five minutes later: a routine IBKR reconnect/farm blip that recovered by itself. No data was lost — every option_snapshots run that day succeeded (0 failed of 82) and the SLIs were met.

The data volume is full: every collector run writes its raw file and fails immediately with OSError(28, 'No space left on device'). This is not a connectivity or Gateway problem — the runs fail in ~2 s at the write step, and all six datasets (option_snapshots, index_snapshots, equity_bars, daily_bars, corporate_actions, assets) hit the same errno.

A second process — /usr/local/bin/python3.12, PID 4127 — held an open handle on /opt/airflow/data/curated.duckdb when the eod dbt build ran at ~17:30 ET, so dbt could not take DuckDB's single-writer lock and the build failed. This is a modelling-layer failure only: collection was unaffected (raw/staged Parquet is written by the collectors, not through DuckDB), and today's 257 pipeline runs include 0 failures.

Alpaca rejected every request with HTTP 401 Unauthorized, so no equity bars (and no daily bars) were collected on 2026-11-12. Credentials were valid through the previous session; the auth failure starts with the first intraday slot today, which points at the Alpaca API keys (expired/revoked/rotated or missing from the task environment) rather than at IBKR or the host.

Option snapshots still run and "succeed", but no quotes are returned: every option_snapshots run on 2026-11-12 carries IBKR error 10197 with two_sided=0, ask_only=0 and bid_only=0 (no_quote=3400 per run), and index_snapshots shows the same 10197 code. 10197 is "market data not subscribed / live data held by another session of the same user" - i.e. a market-data permission or competing-session problem at the Gateway, not a collection or scheduling failure (0 failed runs, durations normal at median ~266 s). The same code on index_snapshots is consistent with a session-wide permission/session condition rather than a single-chain issue. Note: the run/details payloads did not include explicit 354/10089/10090/10167/10168 subscription codes, so the specific subscription-vs-competing-session split is inferred from 10197 alone. SLIs still read 100% coverage / 99.23% on-time over 5 sessions because rows are being written; the emptiness shows up in quote_status, not in the SLIs.

No runs were executed or recorded at all after 2026-11-11 17:31:14 ET: the collector host (Docker/Airflow and therefore the watchdog cards) went down for the whole 2026-11-12 session and had not come back by 2026-11-13 either. This is not a Gateway or vendor failure — nothing in pipeline_runs shows a connection, subscription or Alpaca error, because no task ever ran. Note that pipeline_runs can't distinguish "host down" from "runs recorded on another machine"; the absence of even the 08:00 watchdog cards in Discord is what favours host/Docker/Airflow being down.

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service stopped answering, so contract lookups hung instead of failing fast: the 08:20 Gateway check's "合约查询" step timed out at its 20 s limit, and the 09:10–09:25 option_snapshots runs blew their whole 360 s budget with TimeoutError on every chain. Index snapshots in the same slots also had no underlying price and failed at 120 s. The stall cleared on its own — options slots before 09:10 and from 09:30 onward were normal — so this is a secdef stall, not a Gateway wedge or a data-farm loss (no 1100/2103/2105/2157 codes in the morning runs).

All six option_snapshot slots from 11:00 to 11:25 died at exactly the 480 s (8 min) execution timeout, so Airflow killed them before they raised an error — that is why there is no error message. Each run hung for its whole budget (the shape of a single IBKR quote request that never answered, gateway.md sections A–B / stale-snapshots "every chain failed ... TimeoutError after ~6 min"). The data does not settle whether the Gateway was wedged for that half hour, was briefly unresponsive, or was slow on a request — index_snapshots has no run records at all today, so the "options and indices together" signal is unavailable. Recovery was automatic from 11:30 (runs back to 5-min cadence, median 266 s); no data-farm codes beyond a routine 2103 appear in the later runs, so reconnecting the farms is not indicated.

IBKR's market-data farms for the option/index subscriptions dropped (error codes 2103 and 2105) from 13:00 to 13:25 ET, leaving SPX without a spot price, so each of the six 5-min option_snapshots slots failed fast (~25 s) with RuntimeError('SPX: no spot price'); the collector sent RECONNECTDATA itself and it reported OK, and the farms, now returning 2104 for the successful runs, recovered at 13:30 without a gateway restart, i.e. a transient farm disconnect blip (the same warning codes also appeared on the otherwise successful index_snapshots runs, so the loss shows up as the option runs' no-spot failures rather than a wedged Gateway).

IB Gateway was restarting and waiting on second-factor authentication, not wedged: "Second Factor Authentication initiated" at 08:58 ET with no "Login has completed" until 10:17 ET, so the API refused connections for ~79 min. Every option and index snapshot slot from 09:10 to 10:15 was attempted, failed fast (~4 s, not a hang — no 300 s request timeout, no run-budget exhaustion) with TimeoutError(), and collection recovered on its own from the first slot after login completed. No secdef stall, farm disconnection or subscription problem is in evidence.

Alpaca answered every equity_bars run on 2026-11-12 (90/90 success, none failed), but each run reports bars missing for the same window (from ~12:45 ET to the close); the 17:30 eod refetch re-pulled the last 10 sessions (2026-11-05 … 2026-11-12, plus 2026-11-09/11-10) and each still reports missing_bars=450, so the gap is on the vendor side and the automatic refetch does not recover it. The data is not lost irrevocably — bars are only delayed/gapped at the vendor and can be re-backfilled (runbook backfill for gaps older than 10 sessions) — but it is currently absent and SLI 3 is not met.

A single IBKR request hung in the 11:00 ET option-snapshot run (the run hit the 300 s request timeout and died with TimeoutError() after a 1100/1102 session reconnect), and because normal slots already run ~250-290 s of a 300 s budget, the delay cascaded into the following 11:00-11:30 slots running late. The Gateway API was answering throughout, so this is a hung request, not a frozen or restarting Gateway and not a secdef stall.
